title: Concurrent sampling of transitional and coastal waters by Diffusive Gradient in Thin-films (DGT) and spot sampling for trace metals analysis
author: Bersuder, Amouroux, et al.

steps.title: Prepare sampling equipment
steps.instruction: Wear powder‑free gloves, use clean silicon tubing (never Tygon®), avoid touching sampling ports, keep grease away, and ensure all bottles and accessories are pre‑cleaned for trace‑metal work.

steps.title: Rinse sampler and collect water
steps.instruction: Deploy the water sampler at the planned DGT depth, fill it, discard the water and repeat two more times (three rinses total). After the third rinse, collect water for dissolved‑oxygen (using Winkler or calibrated glass stoppered bottles with preservation if analysed later) and record in‑situ temperature and salinity for DO calculation.

steps.title: Voltammetry sample preparation
steps.instruction: Filter seawater as soon as possible (preferably on‑site) while wearing powder‑free gloves; if on‑site filtration is impossible, store the sample in a cool box with ice packs and filter within 4 h. Rinse a 500 mL HDPE bottle three times with the collected seawater and fill it. Rinse DigiTUBE™ #1 twice with seawater from the HDPE bottle, discard the rinse, then fill DigiTUBE™ #1 with 50 mL (or 100 mL) seawater. Assemble DigiTUBE™ #1 with the DigiFILTER™ and screw DigiTUBE™ #2 onto the opposite side, ensuring a firm seal. Invert the assembly, connect a syringe to the DigiFILTER™ hole, remove the red insert and start filtration, discarding the first 10 mL of filtrate. Filter the remaining 50 mL (or 100 mL) into DigiTUBE™ #2, cap it tightly, then repeat the assembly and filtration steps with DigiTUBE™ #3. If filtration is too slow, replace the DigiFILTER™.

steps.title: Acidify and store voltammetry filtrates
steps.instruction: Immediately after filtration, acidify each filtrate to pH 2 by adding 0.035 mL of 69 % ultrapure HNO₃ per 50 mL sample (or 0.070 mL per 100 mL). Cap the DigiTUBEs, seal if necessary, keep them upright and refrigerate at 4 °C; samples remain stable for several weeks. Transport them in a cool box with ice packs to the analytical laboratory for voltammetry.

steps.title: Prepare voltammetry blanks
steps.instruction: For each site on days 0 and 4, filter two aliquots of 50 mL (or 100 mL) ultrapure water through a pre‑cleaned DigiFILTER™ following the same assembly/filtration steps (5‑6) and then acidify and store them as described in steps 3‑4.

steps.title: ICP‑MS sample preparation
steps.instruction: Collect approximately 100 mL of seawater in a pre‑cleaned, labelled 500 mL HDPE bottle (the remaining water from the 500 mL HDPE bottle used in step 3 can be used). Store the bottle in a cool box with ice packs until shipment to the laboratory.

steps.title: Prepare ICP‑MS blanks
steps.instruction: For each site on days 0 and 4, bring an empty 500 mL HDPE bottle to the field, open it during water collection to expose it to ambient air, then close it after spot sampling. Transport the empty bottle together with the seawater samples in a cool box; in the laboratory open the blank during filtration and close it afterwards.

steps.title: Collect DOC samples
steps.instruction: Rinse a 250 mL pre‑cleaned DURAN® PURE glass bottle three times with water from the sampler, fill it to the brim with no headspace, cap tightly, label clearly, and store cool in the dark until analysis.

steps.title: Prepare DOC blank
steps.instruction: Use de‑ionised water from the analytical laboratory as the DOC blank.

steps.title: Collect SPM samples
steps.instruction: Rinse a 500 mL pre‑cleaned HDPE bottle three times with water from the sampler, collect 500 mL of seawater into the rinsed bottle, cap, label, and store in a cool box for transport to the laboratory.

steps.title: Prepare SPM blank
steps.instruction: Use de‑ionised water from the analytical laboratory as the SPM blank.

steps.title: Collect turbidity sample
steps.instruction: If turbidity is not measured in‑situ, collect 100 mL of seawater, refrigerate immediately, and analyse within 48 h of sampling.

steps.title: Prepare turbidity blank
steps.instruction: Use de‑ionised water from the analytical laboratory as the turbidity blank.

steps.title: Record in‑situ parameters
steps.instruction: At each site and sampling time, measure and record depth, temperature (°C), salinity, dissolved oxygen (% and mg L⁻¹), and pH with a calibrated instrument at the DGT deployment depth.

steps.title: Assemble DGT devices
steps.instruction: In a clean laboratory (laminar flow cabinet or plastic bag), assemble each DGT, load it onto a DGT‑holder, protect with a net if required, and store the assembled units (or individual blanks) in sealed plastic bags refrigerated until deployment.

steps.title: Expose and store DGT field blanks
steps.instruction: Open the individual bags, place the DGT field blanks on a clean surface while assembling field DGTs, then return the blanks to their original bags and keep refrigerated; blanks remain exposed during deployment, retrieval, and laboratory holder/DGT disassembly.

steps.title: Dismantle DGTs for extraction
steps.instruction: Wear powder‑free gloves and work in a positive‑pressure laminar flow hood. Dismantle in the order: (i) DGT laboratory blank, (ii) DGT field blank, (iii) deployed DGTs (least to most contaminated). Insert a plastic screwdriver (or a metal screwdriver covered with plastic) into the groove of the cap, twist to break the cap at its weak point. If the cap does not break, use clean tweezers to break the white filter membrane and pull out the gels directly.

steps.title: Retrieve resin gel and elute
steps.instruction: Remove the broken cap, peel off the filter and diffusive gel to expose the resin‑gel layer (or turn the assembly over and take the thin Chelex® layer). Transfer the resin gel with plastic tweezers into a clean sample tube and add 1 mL of 1 M HNO₃. Ensure the gel is fully immersed and let it stand at room temperature for at least 24 h (or a minimum of 2 h on a shaker for urgent analysis).

steps.title: Dilute eluate and store
steps.instruction: After elution, remove the Chelex® resin, pipette an aliquot from the tube into a new clean tube, and dilute at least 10‑fold with ultrapure water to mitigate saline matrix effects. Store the diluted solution refrigerated at 4 °C until trace‑metal analysis by ICP‑MS (or a comparable technique).
